Demonstration 1: scRNA-seq Simulation Evaluation

Source: vignettes/demo-scrna.Rmd
demo-scrna.Rmd

Introduction

In single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), evaluating the quality of simulated count data is important before testing analysis tools such as clustering, batch correction, or differential expression algorithms.

This tutorial shows how to evaluate synthetic scRNA-seq data step-by-step using scSimEval across the curated evaluation measures suite.

1. Loading the Package and Example Dataset

scSimEval includes pre-packaged real and simulated scRNA-seq count matrices (example_scrna):

library(scSimEval)

# Load packaged scRNA-seq example data
data(example_scrna)

# Examine dimensions and structure
cat("Reference scRNA-seq dimensions:", dim(example_scrna$ref), "\n")
#> Reference scRNA-seq dimensions: 60 80
cat("Simulated scRNA-seq dimensions:", dim(example_scrna$sim), "\n")
#> Simulated scRNA-seq dimensions: 60 80
cat("Cell types represented:", levels(example_scrna$cell_types), "\n")
#> Cell types represented: TypeA TypeB
cat("Batches represented:", levels(example_scrna$batch_info), "\n")
#> Batches represented: Batch1 Batch2

The dataset consists of: * ref: Feature-by-cell matrix of real experimental scRNA-seq read counts (60 genes ×\times 80 cells). * sim: Feature-by-cell matrix of simulated counts generated by a simulation method. * cell_types: Factor of cell type labels. * batch_info: Factor of technical batch identifiers.

2. Step-by-Step Category Evaluation

2.1 Distribution Properties & Summary Measures (Categories 1 and 2)

We evaluate how closely the simulated gene expression distributions match the real reference data using evaluate_simulation_accuracy():

unimodal_res <- evaluate_simulation_accuracy(
  ref_data          = example_scrna$ref,
  sim_data          = example_scrna$sim,
  compute_bivariate = FALSE,
  verbose           = FALSE
)
#> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes
#> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes

# Inspect statistical distance metrics for library size
lib_summary <- subset(unimodal_res$metrics_summary_table, Property == "library_size")
head(lib_summary, 6)
#>                    Category     Property         Metric         Value
#> 1 Distributional Properties library_size    Wasserstein 15.0625000000
#> 2 Distributional Properties library_size             KS  0.2125000000
#> 3 Distributional Properties library_size            MAD 15.0000000000
#> 4 Distributional Properties library_size  Bhattacharyya  0.0001188839
#> 5 Distributional Properties library_size Runs_Statistic -1.7447479960
#> 6 Distributional Properties library_size    NN_Mismatch  0.1750000000

2.2 Cell Clustering and Concordance (Category 3)

We evaluate whether the simulated data preserves distinct cell types in unsupervised and supervised clustering using evaluate_clustering_metrics():

clust_res <- evaluate_clustering_metrics(
  data       = example_scrna$sim,
  cell_types = example_scrna$cell_types,
  ref_data   = example_scrna$ref
)

# Preview clustering concordance metrics
cat("Average Silhouette Width (Simulated):", round(clust_res$silhouette, 4), "\n")
#> Average Silhouette Width (Simulated): 0.0034
cat("Neighborhood Purity:", round(clust_res$neighborhood_purity, 4), "\n")
#> Neighborhood Purity: 0.4775
cat("Adjusted Rand Index (ARI):", round(clust_res$ARI, 4), "\n")
#> Adjusted Rand Index (ARI): -0.0098
cat("Normalized Mutual Information (NMI):", round(clust_res$NMI, 4), "\n")
#> Normalized Mutual Information (NMI): 0.0019

2.3 Batch Effects and Confounder Mixing (Category 4)

We test whether technical batch differences are properly mixed without masking biological differences using evaluate_batch_metrics():

batch_res <- evaluate_batch_metrics(
  data       = example_scrna$sim,
  batch_info = example_scrna$batch_info,
  cell_types = example_scrna$cell_types,
  verbose    = FALSE
)

# Preview batch mixing metrics
cat("Batch Silhouette:", round(batch_res$batch_silhouette, 4), "\n")
#> Batch Silhouette: -0.0027
cat("Principal Component Regression (PCR R2):", round(batch_res$pcr_r2, 4), "\n")
#> Principal Component Regression (PCR R2): 0.0095
cat("Cross-Batch Transfer F1:", round(batch_res$cross_batch_F1, 4), "\n")
#> Cross-Batch Transfer F1: 0.5126

2.4 Differential Expression (DEG) Fidelity (Category 5)

We assess marker gene effect sizes and top marker overlap using evaluate_deg_fidelity():

deg_res <- evaluate_deg_fidelity(
  ref_data      = example_scrna$ref,
  sim_data      = example_scrna$sim,
  ref_celltypes = example_scrna$cell_types,
  sim_celltypes = example_scrna$cell_types
)
#> Biological replicate annotations ('batch_ref' / 'batch_sim') not provided: skipping scRNA-seq Category V pseudobulk DE analysis.

# Display DEG summary metrics
head(deg_res$deg_summary_table)
#> data frame with 0 columns and 0 rows

2.5 Trajectory and Lineage Topology (Category VII — dynverse Workflow)

Following Saelens et al. (2019), evaluate_trajectory_metrics() runs 3-MAD QC and scran HVG filtering before inferring milestone MST trajectories and computing him, edge_flip, geodesic_correlation, F1_branches, and wcor_features:

traj_res <- evaluate_trajectory_metrics(
  ref_data       = example_scrna$ref,
  sim_data       = example_scrna$sim,
  cell_types_ref = example_scrna$cell_types,
  cell_types_sim = example_scrna$cell_types,
  num_trees      = 500L
)

cat("HIM Topology Similarity:", round(traj_res$him, 4), "\n")
#> HIM Topology Similarity: 1
cat("Edge Flip Similarity:", round(traj_res$edge_flip, 4), "\n")
#> Edge Flip Similarity: 1
cat("Geodesic Distance Correlation:", round(traj_res$geodesic_correlation, 4), "\n")
#> Geodesic Distance Correlation: 0.4849
cat("Branch Assignment F1:", round(traj_res$F1_branches, 4), "\n")
#> Branch Assignment F1: 1
cat("Feature Importance wCor:", round(traj_res$wcor_features, 4), "\n")
#> Feature Importance wCor: 0.194

3. Master Unimodal Pipeline: evaluate_simulation_accuracy

Instead of running individual steps, execute the entire unimodal evaluation suite in a single coordinated command:

eval_res <- evaluate_simulation_accuracy(
  ref_data          = example_scrna$ref,
  sim_data          = example_scrna$sim,
  elapsed_time      = 12.5,
  memory_mb         = 340.2,
  compute_bivariate = FALSE,
  verbose           = FALSE
)
#> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes
#> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes

# Preview tidy evaluation summary
head(eval_res$metrics_summary_table)
#>                    Category     Property         Metric         Value
#> 1 Distributional Properties library_size    Wasserstein 15.0625000000
#> 2 Distributional Properties library_size             KS  0.2125000000
#> 3 Distributional Properties library_size            MAD 15.0000000000
#> 4 Distributional Properties library_size  Bhattacharyya  0.0001188839
#> 5 Distributional Properties library_size Runs_Statistic -1.7447479960
#> 6 Distributional Properties library_size    NN_Mismatch  0.1750000000

4. Diagnostic Visualizations

scSimEval includes built-in functions for high-resolution diagnostic plotting:

# 14-Panel Comparative Distribution QC Plot
plot_distribution_qc(
  ref_data = example_scrna$ref,
  sim_data = example_scrna$sim,
  title    = "scRNA-seq Simulation Quality Control"
)

5. Conclusion

This demonstration illustrates how scSimEval comprehensively assesses scRNA-seq simulations across distributions, zero patterns, clustering, batch integration, marker genes, and trajectory dynamics across the curated evaluation measures suite.
